summary: 78-year-old man with a long-term catheter on prednisolone and methotrexate; confusion, rigors, BP 86/50, HR 124, lactate 4.1, cloudy catheter urine.

inputs.hpi: Long-term urethral catheter for 2 years (failed TWOC). Rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and prednisolone 7.5 mg daily for years. Since this morning shaking chills, new confusion, catheter draining cloudy, offensive urine. Carer reports he has hardly passed any urine into the bag today.

exam.general: Drowsy, confused, mottled knees. Pulse 124/min, BP 86/50, RR 26, temperature 38.4°C, SpO2 94% on air.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no peritonism. Catheter bag: 40 mL cloudy urine.

comorbidities: Chronic urinary retention with long-term catheter

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Urosepsis with septic shock (catheter-associated UTI) in an immunosuppressed patient
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Catheter-associated urinary sepsis with hypotension, lactate 4.1 and AKI; on prednisolone and methotrexate.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: The UTI protocol asks for "MSU C&S (mid-stream urine)" in a catheterised man; the catheter change appears only as plan text ("CAUTI: remove or change catheter").
mustInclude.proposedFix: When a catheter is recorded, ask for a catheter specimen after changing the catheter.

mustInclude.note: Prednisolone 7.5 mg for years: adrenal crisis risk in septic shock; parenteral hydrocortisone.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Add immunosuppressant review to the sepsis prompt.

mustExclude.note: Urinary source with a soft abdomen: no laparotomy.

guideline.name: NICE NG51 — Suspected sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management
guideline.section: High-risk criteria (new confusion, SBP ≤90, HR >130, RR ≥25, lactate); blood cultures and broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour for high risk; IV fluid bolus; lactate; senior review; source control
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management. NICE guideline NG51 (updated 2024). London: NICE.

guideline.name: Guidance for the prevention and emergency management of adult patients with adrenal insufficiency (Society for Endocrinology / AAGBI / RCP)
guideline.section: Patients on long-term glucocorticoids (e.g. prednisolone ≥5 mg daily for ≥4 weeks) are at risk of adrenal crisis; during acute illness or sepsis give parenteral hydrocortisone / increased steroid cover
guideline.citation: Simpson H, Tomlinson J, Wass J, Dean J, Arlt W. Guidance for the prevention and emergency management of adult patients with adrenal insufficiency. Clin Med (Lond). 2020;20:371–378.

guideline.name: NICE NG148 — Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management
guideline.section: Detection (creatinine against baseline); urinalysis for all with AKI; ultrasound of the urinary tract within 24 h when obstruction is suspected (immediately if pyonephrosis suspected); stop/withhold nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics) and review metformin; refer to urology immediately for pyonephrosis, obstructed solitary kidney, bilateral upper tract obstruction or complications of obstruction; nephrology referral criteria
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Acute kidney injury: prevention, detection and management. NICE guideline NG148. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: High-risk sepsis (NICE NG51): cultures, IV antibiotics and fluids within the hour; steroid-dependent patients need hydrocortisone cover.
